chapter: Family band and learning to play
title: Lessons from O'Bannon at fifty cents and learning to transpose
summary: O'Bannon offers to teach him to read in exchange for jazz lessons, and teaches transposition.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I didn't say "no," I said, "Yeah, you teach me how to read good and I'll teach you how to play jazz good."

So he had a little studio. He was teaching, too. He had students, all white students, because there weren't many black people trying to learn music, you know, which is sad now. I don't know anybody in Sherman that is learning how to play. So anyway, he says, "You come to see me." I says, "Well, I don't know if I can afford it." He says, "Can you afford 50 cents a lesson?" So I says, "Yeah, I think so." So he says, "Now, you don't have to." I says, "Well, I can."
So we started, because Malone was along with one of those carnivals and he was gone, you know. Sometimes he'd go and stay like six months, a year, something like that, and we didn't see him anymore.

So I started visiting Frank on certain days that he would have off. He played every night, but some days he didn't have to go to work until like 6:30, 7:00. So I'd go out there and the first thing he did was, you know, there was a lot of sheet music then in those days. So he says, "Can you read this?" I said, "Yeah, I can read it." He says, "But you can't play these notes now like with a piano?" I says, "Why not?" He says, "You got to transpose that now, a tone and a half below." I said, "What do you mean?"

I didn't know what I was doing, man. He says, "Transposition or transposing means that -- see, like if that's a A natural on your saxophone, on your alto, that's got to be F sharp on your horn." I says, "Oh, I don't think I can make that." He says, "Oh, yeah. You can make that." So he says, "You just start doing it at home. I'll give you some music. Instead of playing these notes," he says, "just play some low notes and I'll give you something that's got melody to it and you'll know if you're playing right." So that's the way he started me in transposing.
